metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Optics — Definition of Refractive Index of Glass
metadata.note: 3m: define refractive index. Two valid approaches: (1) ratio of speeds: n = speed in vacuum / speed in medium; (2) Snell's law: n = sin(i)/sin(r). Cloze covers both: 'speed of light in air(1m) / speed of light in glass(1m) / sin(angle of incidence)/sin(angle of refraction)(1m)'. Marks split 1+1+1.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q4c — Define Refractive Index of Glass
question.text:
Define the term 'refractive index' of glass by completing the statements below:

Definition 1 (ratio of speeds): The refractive index of glass is the ratio of the [[1]] to the [[2]].

Definition 2 (Snell's law): The refractive index is also equal to [[3]].
question.general_feedback:
Refractive index (n) of glass:

Definition 1: n = speed of light in air (vacuum) / speed of light in glass

Definition 2 (Snell's law): n = sin(angle of incidence) / sin(angle of refraction) = sin(i) / sin(r)

Key values: n > 1 for glass (light slows down when entering a denser medium). For CSEC Physics, n_glass = 1.5 typically.

Note: Since n = c_air / c_glass and c_glass < c_air, n > 1 for all optical materials.

ddwtos.cloze_html:
Definition 1: The refractive index of glass is the ratio of the [[1]] to the [[2]].

Definition 2: The refractive index is also equal to [[3]].

groups.label: Refractive index = ___ (numerator)
groups.diagnostic_hint: n = speed of light in air (or vacuum) ÷ speed of light in medium. The numerator is the speed in the LESS DENSE medium (air/vacuum = 3 × 10⁸ m/s).

groups.label: Refractive index = speed in air ÷ ___ (denominator)
groups.diagnostic_hint: The denominator is the speed of light in the GLASS (the denser medium). Since light slows down in glass, n > 1 for all transparent materials.

options.text: sin(angle of incidence) / sin(angle of refraction)

groups.label: Refractive index also equals ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: Snell's Law: n = sin(i)/sin(r), where i is the angle of incidence (in air) and r is the angle of refraction (in glass). Both angles are measured from the normal.

word_bank: sin(angle of incidence) / sin(angle of refraction)
ddwtos.word_bank_note: 10 tokens for 3 slots. Slot 1 (numerator = air/vacuum speed): both air and vacuum are accepted — in CSEC context, speed in air ≈ speed in vacuum. 'Speed in glass' in the numerator gives n < 1 (incorrect for glass). 'Wavelength' — wavelength changes with medium but defining n as a wavelength ratio is not the CSEC definition. Slot 2 (denominator = glass speed): 'Speed in air' in the denominator would give n < 1 (inverted). 'Frequency' does not change with medium — not a valid denominator. Slot 3 (Snell's ratio): both phrasings accepted (sin(i)/sin(r) or the full description). 'sin(r)/sin(i)' is inverted — would give n < 1. 'cos' terms are used in different optical formulas.
